killington.note: Good morning, Beast family, We're due for more soft, spring-y conditions out there today, as some showers rolled through last night to saturate our surfaces even further. The clouds will roll away for parts of this afternoon, with temps climbing into the mid-50s and a steady north wind keeping things feeling crisp on the hill. Spring is still in full swing out there, with conditions and coverage evolving by the day, but the skiing & riding is still delivering across the mountain. Conditions today should consist of wet snow and wet granular with a firmer base underneath. As we roll deeper into the season, more thin spots and short walks are starting to show up, but our grooming crew is out there every night doing their best to keep things stitched together. Unfortunately, the combination of warm & wet weather is taking out some of our connecting trails, so access from the top of K-1 to the top of North Ridge will only be available via the Peak Walkway. Access from K-1 to Superstar is still available via Blue Heaven, but be aware of variable conditions, thin cover, and additional areas of walking required along Launch Pad. Great Northern is now closed below Mouse Trap, so the terrain off of K-1 and Snowdon is now for advanced skiers & riders only. If you would like to access the terrain at Ramshead, we recommend parking at Ramshead and proceeding to the lift. Caper remains open for skiing and riding back to the Snowdon Six and K-1 Gondola from Ramshead as conditions allow, though you will not be able to ski back to Ramshead. Easy Street is no longer fully connected from top-to-bottom, though Timberline is still open and firing for all your park skiing & riding needs. Our grooming team took snow where it still lingers on closed trails and moving it to areas like Great Northern and Killink. Mouse Run, Lower Bunny Buster, and Chute. Superstar has been a blast to rip with a flowy ride higher up and legit moguls on the lower pitch. Upper Skyelark and Lower Bittersweet provide more of a cruise if you’re after a chill run. If you want to find the best coverage we have out there, the Superstar Six is what you'll want to be lapping. Check the Lifts & Trails Report for your full list of groomed options. We’ll be spinning 5 lifts today, with the Superstar Six, K-1 Gondola, Snowdon Six, and Ramshead Express opening at 9:00 a.m., with the North Ridge Quad joining at 9:30 a.m. While we did everything we could to stretch the snow, Bear Mountain and Needles Eye won’t be offering skiing and riding this weekend. A stretch of warm temperatures, periods of rain, and a lack of late-season natural snowfall have taken their toll, reducing coverage in those areas to the point where skiing and riding is no longer possible. We’ll be saying goodbye to Bear and Needles Eye for the season, but not without a solid run. Due to coverage in other parts of the mountain, this will be the last weekend of the season for the Ramshead Quad, Snowdon Six, North Ridge Quad, and the K-1 Gondola. The Superstar Six will continue running as long as conditions allow. Starting this Saturday, April 18th, Superstar will begin running until 5:00 p.m. on Saturdays. On the kparks front, Timberline continues to shine with close to 23 features including a halfpipe. Our Parks Crew recently refreshed features ahead of the Spring Send-Off, so it’s still a great spot to take a few laps. Check the Terrain Parks Report for the full details. While many mountains across the East have wrapped up their seasons, we’re still getting after it with plenty of terrain and more spring skiing and spectacular events ahead. This Saturday, April 18th is our Dazed and Defrosted spring music festival and Winter Season Pass Holder Appreciation Party . Put it on your radar and we'll catch you at The Beast. Have fun out there! - Cullen Operating Day: 157 Season passes for 26/27 are now on sale! Lock in the lowest price on Beast 365 or Winter Unlimited passes with lots of perks, plus free skiing & riding for the rest of this spring. copper mountain.note: Happy Friday! The season has been extended! Copper's new closing day will be May 3rd. Be sure to check out Copper's Instagram page or website for up-to-date information. Today will be mostly cloudy with light snow falling from late morning into this evening. Be sure to layer up as the temperature will be dropping throughout the day into single digits tonight. Winds will be out of the west around 10-15 mph, gusting into the 30s. Lots of great events taking place this weekend such as Copper Live and Peace Out in Central Park. Check the Copper events page for more information: https://www.coppercolorado.com/events-activities/events-calendar/

snowbird.note: Good morning pookies! It’s your occasional bestie / snow reporter Lauren. Winter really said, “I bet you thought you'd seen the last of me” and honestly… we’re not mad about it. The Bird picked up 7” overnight , with storm totals landing right around 8” . It’s giving soft turns, sneaky powder pockets and full delulu spring-winter crossover energy. Temps stayed nice and chilly overnight, so things are skiing way more mid-winter than mid-April. Groomers = dreamy. Off-piste = soft with a little spice. Visibility might be doing its usual “mystery box” thing, so keep the goggles ready for anything from flat light to surprise hero moments. Winter may be on its encore, but surf season is still very much in her main character era. And this weekend? We’ve got a stacked lineup for Electronic Music Plazapalooza . Whether you rave or think you don’t rave yet … this might be your origin story. While we can’t require glitter and party fits at a FREE concert, we strongly encourage it. Somehow it’s mid-April (??), which means Mother’s Day is May 10 . Don’t procrastinate. Be better than that. Pretend you’ve learned from your mistakes. Lock in reservations for Mother’s Day Brunch at The Aerie now and earn yourself serious gold stars. Future you—and the mom(s) in your life—will thank you. Housekeeping: Note 1: Gadzoom, Gad 2, Wilbere, and Baldy are closing for the season on Monday, April 20. It’s not goodbye… it’s ski you next season. Note 2: Spring hours go into effect Monday, April 20: Tram + Little Cloud: 8 AM – 2 PM Mineral: 8 AM – 1 PM Peruvian: 8 AM – 2 PM (Fri–Sun) Peruvian Tunnel: 8 AM – 1 PM (Fri–Sun) Note 3: Chickadee Bowl is CLOSED for construction. If you usually park there, try the bypass road past Entry 4. Note 4: ALL uphill travel is closed. Don’t be that guy (or gal). Note 5: And as always—ski and ride in control… or you’re gonna have a bad time. I’m proud of you!! Hope you have a great weekend—you deserve it. XOXO, Gossip Girl 🐦
